text:
Asha Patel: flagging a high-priority customer ticket — they removed a bunch of Okta groups last night but users still have product roles in Redwood. customer: acme-analytics.
Marco Reyes: do we have logs from the SCIM service for that org? any 403s or errors?
Asha Patel: support-bot pulled logs. saw repeated 403s on /scim/v2/Groups and /scim/v2/Users/bulk around 03:14 UTC. message: "insufficient_scope". customer says they rotated their SCIM token ~02:50 UTC.
support-bot: [automated] recent events for org acme-analytics:
- 2024-11-06T02:50:12Z Okta -> SCIM token rotated (okta-admin)
- 2024-11-06T03:12:03Z PATCH /scim/v2/Groups - 403 {"error":"insufficient_scope"}
- 2024-11-06T03:12:07Z PATCH /scim/v2/Groups - 403 {"error":"insufficient_scope"}
- 2024-11-06T03:14:30Z DELETE /scim/v2/Groups/{id} - 204 (retry)
- 2024-11-06T03:15:01Z POST /admin/v1/role-assignments - 200 (internal)

Samir Chen: ok that suggests new token missing a scope we rely on. which scopes do we require?
Elena Voss: our SCIM integration expects scopes: Users.read, Users.write, Groups.read, Groups.write, and ServiceAccount.manage (for webhook/metadata updates). if Groups.write missing, group membership changes may not apply.
Marco Reyes: customer support shows their token metadata: only Users.read, Users.write, Groups.read. Groups.write omitted.
Asha Patel: so token rotation removed Groups.write. Okta team says they intentionally limited scopes for security. customer expected Redwood to still process deprovisions that had been queued.
Samir Chen: partially true — we enqueue membership deltas on receipt of group change events. when we try to apply them against SCIM API with insufficient scope we get 403 and mark as failed. background workers retry with exponential backoff but after N failures they’re flagged and require manual intervention.
Asha Patel: they called us — ~120 users still have the product "analyst" role that should have been removed. they want an immediate cleanup.
Elena Voss: remediation path: 1) ask customer to re-issue a SCIM token with Groups.write. 2) we can run a one-off backfill job that reconciles Okta group membership vs role assignments. 3) optionally support can run a temporary admin fix to remove roles via internal admin API if they want faster.
Marco Reyes: can we run the backfill without exposing anything? what's the safety checks?
Samir Chen: backfill plan: query current Okta group membership using the customer's Okta snapshots (they provided a CSV export), compute delta of users who lost group membership, then invoke our internal role-removal API per user with a rate limit cap of 200 reqs/s and a dry-run option. we also record audit entries for each removal.
Asha Patel: customer asked if this was caused by a mapping change. note: they migrate group names to a new naming convention at 02:30; some groups had externalId changed in the migration.
Elena Voss: that can complicate things — we support two mapping modes in our SCIM connector: match by group.externalId (preferred) or group.displayName. if externalId changes and they switched to matching by externalId, old membership won't be found. but that produces missing-group warnings rather than 403. different issue than insufficient_scope.
Marco Reyes: got it. so we have two factors: token scopes causing failed apply attempts, and externalId rename causing some deltas to not match. both could contribute to the partially-deprovisioned state.
Samir Chen: reproduced locally with a reduced flow:
```bash
# simulate Okta -> our webhook queue then worker apply
curl -X POST https://scim.redwood.test/webhook -H 'Authorization: Bearer fake' -d '{"event":"group.removed","group":{"id":"g-123","displayName":"analytics-team"}}'
# worker tries to call provider with token missing Groups.write
HTTP/1.1 403 
{"error":"insufficient_scope","required_scopes":["Groups.write"]}
```
Samir Chen: when the worker sees that response we log the required_scopes into the task metadata. we currently do not auto-open an escalation.
Asha Patel: customer asked for timeline — how long to fix if they supply a corrected token now?
Samir Chen: if they update token now and we re-run the pending queue items we can clear most users inside ~18 minutes (queue depth ~1200 events, worker capacity). backfill via CSV is faster for this specific case — maybe 6-10 minutes plus manual review.
Elena Voss: proposed immediate steps for support to follow:
- tell customer to generate a SCIM token including Groups.write and share it via secure channel.
- we will rotate their token on our side and re-enqueue failed tasks.
- run a dry-run backfill and show them the delta (CSV) before any writes.
- upon approval run the removal job with audit logging.

Marco Reyes: also adding a short-term product change: when we detect 403 with required_scopes in the response, surface a support alert and mark the org as 'scim-limited-scope' in console so admins see why provisioning is degraded. file a follow-up ticket to add an automated self-serve token-scope-check in settings.
Asha Patel: customer accepted that path. they provided a new token with Groups.write at 03:56 UTC.
support-bot: [automated] token rotation applied by support at 2024-11-06T03:58:01Z; requeuing 124 failed tasks.
Samir Chen: started requeue, saw success rate ~95% for group removals, 6 items failed due to missing user record (externalId mismatch) and 1 failed due to rate-limit backoff.
Elena Voss: for the 6 users: we need to coordinate with Okta to get the historical externalIds. recommend a short CSV reconcile with customer.
Marco Reyes: logging action items: 1) support: send dry-run CSV and ask for sign-off. 2) eng/infra: add alert for 403-insufficient_scope and UI banner. 3) eng-ml? not relevant. 4) product: backlog self-check token-scopes in integration settings.
Asha Patel: thanks everyone. I'll post the customer communications and confirm once backfill runs. :thumbsup:
Samir Chen: notes for postmortem: consider making retries smarter when required_scopes returned (don’t backoff long — escalate instead). also consider a reconciliation job that periodically compares SCIM group data vs role assignments to avoid long-lived drift.
Elena Voss: and document mapping pitfalls: externalId vs displayName and explain consequences in our integration docs.
Asha Patel: closing loop — customer confirmed roles removed after the run, they were happy with audit logs. marking resolved. :party_parrot:
support-bot: [automated] thread closed by Asha Patel at 2024-11-06T04:25:05Z
